<h2 id="current-errno"><code>CurrentErrno</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CurrentErrno() -> int64
```

The calling thread's current `errno` value.
Takes nothing and returns the value by copy. Meaningful only immediately after a call that failed: nothing on
Darwin clears it on success, so a value left over from an earlier failure is still there.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/Errors.rux#L154)

**Returns**: the calling thread's current `errno`

<h2 id="normalize"><code>Normalize</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Normalize(result: int64) -> int64
```

Folds a libSystem result and the thread's `errno` into one value.
`result` is read by value. A result of `-1` becomes the negative of whatever `errno` holds; anything else is
returned unchanged. That is what makes every wrapper in this package report the way the Linux and FreeBSD ones
do, so a caller reads all three with [`IsError`](/docs/api/macos/errors#is-error) and [`Errno`](/docs/api/macos/errors#errno).
A call that legitimately returns `-1` would be misread, which is why nothing here wraps one.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/Errors.rux#L167)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type    | Description                  |
| -------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| `result` | `int64` | the libSystem result to fold |

**Returns**: the result unchanged, or the negative of `errno` when it was -1

<h2 id="is-error"><code>IsError</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsError(result: int64) -> bool
```

Whether a normalized result is one of the reserved error values.
`result` is read by value. True for `-4095` through `-1`.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/Errors.rux#L179)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type    | Description            |
| -------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `result` | `int64` | the raw result to test |

**Returns**: whether it is one of the reserved error values

<h2 id="errno"><code>Errno</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Errno(result: int64) -> int64
```

The error number a normalized result carries, or zero when it carries none.
`result` is read by value; the number is returned positive, as a man page names it.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/Errors.rux#L189)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type    | Description            |
| -------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| `result` | `int64` | the raw result to read |

**Returns**: the error number, positive, or zero when the result carries none
